newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Automakers minorities to get 411 cts payout. [CORRECTED 09:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Automakers minorities to get 411 cts payout. [CORRECTED 09:56 GMT]

text.p: South African car maker Automakers Ltd said on Monday it planned to delist under a proposed scheme which would bring in an unnamed international company.
Minority shareholders will receive a consideration of 411 cents a share, the company said in a statement.
The buyout price represents a 76 percent premium to the average closing price of the share over the last 20 (Corrects from two) days.
Automakers' shares soared at the end of last week -- ending Friday at 330 cents -- as the company issued a cautionary notice that certain developments were under consideration.

The stock market has been awash with rumours that Japan's Nissan Motor Co Ltd and Italy's Fiat were contemplating taking a stake in the company, which manufactures and markets their models in South Africa.
Fiat denied any interest in Automakers while Nissan declined to comment, leaving the Japanese concern as the firm favourite in the minds of many market players.
Automakers chief executive John Newbury told Business Day newspaper he would like to see the Japanese take a stake but said nothing had been concluded.

Under the scheme, Automakers' majority shareholder Sankorp -- which holds 50.7 percent of the issued share capital -- will make the payout to minorities ahead of bringing in the international concern.
Mitsui Ltd, which holds 8.7 percent, and Nissan Diesel Co Ltd, with 4.3 percent, would continue to hold such shares in Automakers after the change-over, the company said.

Automakers said it had asked Sankorp to make an offer to minorities in view of the tough trading conditions since the company's listing in October 1995 and the fact that prospects were unlikely to improve in the short to medium term.
- the rand's 28 percent deterioration against the dollar and 25 percent fall against the lira in the last 12 months;
- no increase in the selling price of vehicles, for all practical purposes;
- a significant increase in imported models;
- a deteroriation in gross margins due to the expansion of the entry level of the market and increased competitiveness;
"The aforegoing factors have resulted in significant market share loss by Automakers with a corresponding negative impact on profitability," the statement said.
